concept_uz: Har bir gʻildirak, lagan va gumbazda aylana diametrdan «uch martadan sal koʻp». Nisbat xalqi bu sonni kasr qilolmaydi. Olim Pi keladi — lekin gapini hech qachon tugatolmaydi, butun saroy uxlab qoladi. Uning raqamlari takrorlanmaydi: «Ismim nisbatdan, lekin men Nisbat xalqidan emasman».
style_line: Premium 3D animated feature film style, gentle split light — cool moonlight from the left, warm sunlight from the right — soft shadows, rich colours, vertical 9:16. No text, no captions, no letters or numerals written anywhere, no watermark.

refs.prompt: Vertical 9:16 full-body character portrait. A round king shaped like a thick, chunky upright ring with a small hole in the middle, so its wide front face is a disc. The ring is coloured like a yin-yang: the left half dark moon-silver with one small bright gold dot, the right half bright sun-gold with one small dark silver dot, the two halves curving into each other in a smooth S-shaped wave — made of polished metal, not a flat printed symbol. Big kind expressive eyes and a small mouth on the front of the ring, thin cartoon arms and legs, a small jewelled crown tilted to the left, holding a long plain wooden staff. He stands in the middle of a vast low-poly crystal plain, exactly where the cool left side meets the warm right side, front view, centred.

Vertical 9:16 full-body character portrait. A slim upright sun-gold character shaped like a tall narrow pillar with a small slanted flag-like tip at the top, big cheerful eyes, a wide smile, thin cartoon arms and legs, and a small round badge with a plus sign pinned on its chest. It stands on the vast low-poly crystal plain, front view, centred.

Change this character: exactly the same shape, size and face, but made of shining moon-silver instead of gold, eyebrows lowered in a grumpy frown, arms crossed, and a horizontal dark-blue sash wrapped across its middle instead of the plus badge. Same plain, same framing, full body, front view.

Vertical 9:16 wide landscape. A vast empty low-poly crystal plain made of smooth faceted triangular polygons: cool lavender-blue facets on the left, warm amber facets on the right, blending softly in the middle. A thin glowing straight path runs across the ground from left to right through the centre. The sky is split the same gentle way: soft twilight indigo with a few stars on the left, where a pale moon with a gentle old woman's face smiles; warm morning light on the right, where a big warm sun with a kind old grandfather's face — smiling eyes, bushy eyebrows and a beard of rays — smiles back. Not dark, just a gentle difference between the two sides. No characters.

Vertical 9:16 full-body character portrait. An elderly scholar character with a round kind face, small spectacles and a long white beard, wearing a deep-blue chapan robe covered in a pattern of circles, holding a coil of measuring rope. He stands beside a wooden cart wheel on the low-poly crystal plain, front view, centred.

On this low-poly crystal plain, a wheelwright character in a leather apron measures a big wooden cart wheel with a rope; around him lie a large round serving plate, a clay tandir oven and, in the distance, a turquoise dome. Vertical 9:16.

scenes.prompt: Slow push-in across the wheelwright's workshop: a cart wheel, a round plate, a clay pot, a dome in the distance. An off-screen narrator says in Uzbek with a calm, deep, velvety storyteller's voice, slow and mysterious like an old radio fairy tale: "Saltanatdagi har bir g'ildirak, har bir lagan bitta sirni yashirar ekan…" Lip-sync: nobody on screen speaks — the narrator is heard off screen and every mouth stays closed. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Saltanatdagi har bir gʻildirak, har bir lagan bitta sirni yashirar ekan…

scenes.prompt: The wheelwright wraps the rope once around the wheel, then lays the rope straight across the wheel's width: it fits three times and a little bit more. He scratches his head and says in Uzbek with a gruff, friendly voice of an old craftsman: "Yana uch martadan sal ko'p!" Lip-sync: only the wheelwright moves its mouth and speaks; every other character keeps its mouth closed and just listens. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

Quick comic montage: characters measure the round plate, the tandir's mouth and the dome with ropes — each time the rope fits three times and a little more. Together they says in Uzbek with a crowd of cheerful mixed voices in unison: "Har safar uchdan sal ko'p!" Lip-sync: only the whole crowd, together moves its mouth and speaks; every other character keeps its mouth closed and just listens. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

The fraction folk proudly bring a fraction to the wheel; it almost matches but sticks out a tiny bit. One of them says in Uzbek with several proud young voices speaking in unison: "Yigirma ikki bo'lu yetti!" and another, disappointed, says in Uzbek with a low, raspy, sulky voice of a grumpy ten-year-old boy, slow, with a sigh: "Sal ko'p!" Lip-sync: the lines are spoken in this order — one of the fraction characters, then the silver character with the dark-blue sash; each mouth moves only during its own line and everyone else keeps their mouth closed. No subtitles, no on-screen text.
At the palace gate the elderly scholar in the circle-patterned robe arrives slowly, leaning on his coil of measuring rope; the crowd parts respectfully. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

The ring-king asks hopefully, says in Uzbek with a deep, warm, slightly theatrical baritone voice of a kind middle-aged king, slow, with dramatic pauses: "Doiraning sirini bilasizmi?" The scholar clears his throat and says in Uzbek with a slow, sleepy, creaky voice of an elderly professor: "Doiraning sirini aytsam… uch butun, bir, to'rt, bir, besh, to'qqiz…" Lip-sync: the lines are spoken in this order — the yin-yang ring-king, then the elderly scholar in the circle-patterned robe; each mouth moves only during its own line and everyone else keeps their mouth closed. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Doiraning sirini aytsam… uch butun, bir, toʻrt, bir, besh, toʻqqiz…

scenes.prompt: Time-lapse through the night: the whole palace falls asleep one by one, the silver character yawning hugely and toppling over, snoring; the scholar is still talking, says in Uzbek with a slow, sleepy, creaky voice of an elderly professor: "…ikki, olti, besh, uch, besh, sakkiz…" Lip-sync: only the elderly scholar in the circle-patterned robe moves its mouth and speaks; every other character keeps its mouth closed and just listens. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

Morning. The ring-king wakes up and asks, says in Uzbek with a deep, warm, slightly theatrical baritone voice of a kind middle-aged king, slow, with dramatic pauses: "Hech bo'lmasa, takrorlanadimi?" The scholar shakes his head kindly: says in Uzbek with a slow, sleepy, creaky voice of an elderly professor: "Yo'q. Hech qachon takrorlanmaydi, hech qachon tugamaydi." Lip-sync: the lines are spoken in this order — the yin-yang ring-king, then the elderly scholar in the circle-patterned robe; each mouth moves only during its own line and everyone else keeps their mouth closed. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Yoʻq. Hech qachon takrorlanmaydi, hech qachon tugamaydi.

scenes.prompt: Sunset. The scholar bows and walks away toward the dark horizon with his rope, turning back once to says in Uzbek with a slow, sleepy, creaky voice of an elderly professor: "Ismim nisbatdan, lekin men Nisbat xalqidan emasman." An off-screen narrator says in Uzbek with a calm, deep, velvety storyteller's voice, slow and mysterious like an old radio fairy tale: "Davomi — powerty.uz da." Lip-sync: only the elderly scholar in the circle-patterned robe moves its mouth and speaks; every other character keeps its mouth closed and just listens. The narrator is heard off screen: no one on screen moves their lips for it. No subtitles, no on-screen text.

lines.text: Ismim nisbatdan, lekin men Nisbat xalqidan emasman.
